questions.question: Which country does LEGO come from?
questions.explanation: LEGO began in the Danish town of Billund, where there is now a LEGOLAND park.

questions.question: The name LEGO comes from two words meaning what?
questions.explanation: It is short for leg godt, which is Danish for play well.

questions.question: In chess, which piece can only ever move diagonally?
questions.explanation: Because it only moves diagonally, a bishop stays on the same colour square for the whole game.

questions.question: How many squares are there on a chessboard?
questions.explanation: A chessboard has eight rows of eight squares, alternating light and dark.

questions.question: In which country was the Rubik's Cube invented?
questions.explanation: Erno Rubik was a design teacher in Budapest, and he first called his puzzle the Magic Cube.

questions.question: Which is the most expensive property on a UK Monopoly board?
questions.explanation: Mayfair costs 400 pounds to buy, the most of any square on the board.

questions.question: Snakes and Ladders was first played in which country?
questions.explanation: In India it was a game about good and bad deeds, where ladders were good deeds and snakes were bad ones.

questions.question: When Mr Potato Head first went on sale in 1952, what did children push its pieces into?
questions.explanation: The kit was just eyes, noses, mouths and ears, and a plastic potato body was not included until 1964.

questions.question: What is the name of Barbie's boyfriend?
questions.explanation: Ken first appeared in 1961, two years after Barbie.

questions.question: Which game is played by throwing a small ball and scooping up little metal star-shaped pieces?
questions.explanation: Long ago the game was played with small animal bones or stones, which is why it is also called knucklebones.

questions.question: How many dots are there altogether on a normal six-sided dice?
questions.explanation: One plus two plus three plus four plus five plus six makes 21, and opposite sides always add up to seven.

questions.question: In the card game UNO, how many cards does each player start with?
questions.explanation: Each player gets seven cards, and you must shout UNO when you are down to your last one.

questions.question: Teddy bears are named after which American president?
questions.explanation: President Theodore Roosevelt, known as Teddy, refused to shoot a bear on a hunting trip, and a toy maker named a bear after him.

questions.question: In Scrabble, which two letters are worth the most points?
questions.explanation: Q and Z score 10 points each, while J and X score 8.

questions.question: Which toy was invented by an engineer who watched a spring tumble off a shelf?
questions.explanation: Richard James saw a spring keep moving after it fell, and the Slinky went on sale in 1945.

questions.question: In which year did Erno Rubik invent his famous cube?
questions.explanation: He made the first one in 1974, and it took him about a month to solve it himself.

questions.question: On the UK Monopoly board, what colour is the set that includes Trafalgar Square?
questions.explanation: Trafalgar Square shares the red set with the Strand and Fleet Street.

questions.question: Monopoly grew out of which earlier game, patented by Lizzie Magie in 1904?
questions.explanation: Lizzie Magie designed it to show the unfairness of landlords growing rich from rents.

questions.question: In which year was Barbie launched?
questions.explanation: Barbie was launched at the American International Toy Fair in New York in March 1959.

questions.question: Which chess opening begins with the moves e4 e5, Nf3 Nc6, Bb5?
questions.explanation: It is named after a 16th-century Spanish priest, which is why it is also called the Spanish Opening.

questions.question: Who beat Boris Spassky in Reykjavik in 1972 to become world chess champion?
questions.explanation: Fischer's win, at the height of the Cold War, was dubbed the Match of the Century.

questions.question: Which IBM computer beat Garry Kasparov at chess in 1997?
questions.explanation: It was the first time a computer had beaten a reigning world champion in a full match.

questions.question: What is the board game Cluedo called in the USA?
questions.explanation: Cluedo was invented in Birmingham by Anthony Pratt, its name a mix of clue and Ludo.

questions.question: In which country was Trivial Pursuit invented?
questions.explanation: Two friends in Montreal came up with it in 1979 after finding pieces missing from their Scrabble set.

questions.question: Which talking toy, a huge hit in 1998, seemed to learn English as time went on?
questions.explanation: Each Furby started out speaking its own language, Furbish, and was programmed to use more English over time.

questions.question: The Tamagotchi digital pet came from which country?
questions.explanation: Bandai launched it in Japan in 1996, and its name blends the Japanese for egg and watch.

questions.question: Which word game was invented by an out-of-work architect, Alfred Mosher Butts?
questions.explanation: Butts worked out how many of each letter to include by counting letters in newspapers, including the New York Times.

questions.question: Which construction toy was patented in 1901 by Frank Hornby of Liverpool?
questions.explanation: Hornby first called it Mechanics Made Easy, and later went on to make his famous model trains.

questions.question: How many pieces does each player start with in backgammon?
questions.explanation: Each side has 15 checkers to race round the board and bear off.

questions.question: The name Jenga comes from a Swahili word meaning what?
questions.explanation: Its British inventor, Leslie Scott, grew up speaking Swahili in Tanzania and named it after kujenga, to build.
